name: Facet
text: Use Playwright MCP to drive EXCAVA’s interface directly from the MCP server. This keeps the visualization live and interactive without manual clicks, so the screencast stays crisp and real-time. The trade-off is that EXCAVA’s interface must expose stable, testable elements for Playwright to latch onto—no fragile selectors.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The single point of failure isn’t just a crash risk—it’s a *debugging nightmare* if EXCAVA’s interface changes and Playwright breaks silently. A safer bet is to record a clean screencast first, then overlay interactive highlights later; that way, the visualization stays reliable even if the interface shifts. Settle it by testing both: run Playwright against EXCAVA’s live interface for 10 minutes, then compare the screencast output to a pre-recorded baseline.
